main_text.p: τατον Θεῦ οἰκητήριον, Philosophi autē coelum stelliferum appellant, & quod merito Gentiles in stupo-rem, christianos in admiratio-nem dedit, multis varijsquè stel-lis, veluti elegantissimis picturis variegatum esse : ejusquè lucidis-sima lumina diu, noctuquè insi-gnem utilitatem præstare homi-nibus, ex Creatoris ordinatione. Docet quinetiam eadem inva-riabilis observatio, idem maxi-mum opus, super quod Deus de-corem suum posuit, in suo nitore, claritate & ἀεικινήσει hactenus per-stitisse, & perstiturum esse usquè ad terminum illum, quem ὁ τῶν ὅλων ποιητὴς, ut cum Iustino Mar-tyre loquar, ipsi destinavit.

page.notes: The Greek words are printed in Greek letters; the transcription of the Greek is approximate. The catchword "ejus" is printed at the right foot, and the final line of the page is set in larger type. The "(*)" mark is a printed reference mark beside the page number.
